observations.result: No unused files, dependencies or exports reported.
Chronicle, recovery, watcher, storage-protection and stable-identity contracts compile with strict TypeScript checking.

implemented: The Chronicle command runner is Node-safe inside Electron and supports explicit initialization/adoption, offline read-only inspection, diff, selected-path commit review, history, revision-aware file restore, remote setup and explicit ff-only pull/push seams.
Selected Chronicle commits use --only and preserve unrelated staged changes; app-private paths are excluded from the default review and no remote command is run during inspection.

Watcher recovery exposes verified rescans for overflow, sleep and reconnect signals, while stable identity records live outside the vault and survive rename, duplicate creation and same-path replacement.

History retention keeps protected conflicts, reports protected-cap overflow, and provides an explicit cleanup callback; OS storage probes report enabled, disabled or unknown without claiming unverified encryption.
limitations: No live remote pull/push or provisioned external sync backend was attempted; the test remote is offline.invalid and sync calls use an injectable command seam.

Chronicle conflict resolution beyond file-level revision recovery, retention file deletion wiring, uninstall cleanup UI, external-tool matrix certification, cross-platform local filesystem behavior and reference Obsidian reopen tests remain pending.
Electron visible launch/accessibility automation and the packaged Electron/Chromium/Node notice audit remain pending.
